# Grant Wiggins

Grant Wiggins (1950–2015) was an educational reformer whose framework — Understanding by Design (UbD) — reshaped how teachers plan curriculum across the English-speaking world. Co-developed with Jay McTighe, UbD's core insight is deceptively simple: design instruction backward from the evidence of understanding you want to see, not forward from the textbook chapters you need to cover.

Wiggins spent his career attacking what he called "the twin sins of traditional design": activity-oriented teaching (hands-on without minds-on) and coverage-oriented teaching (marching through content without checking whether students understood it). His alternative — backward design — asks three questions before any lesson is planned: What should students understand? What evidence will prove it? What learning experiences will produce that evidence?

His work on authentic assessment anticipated the performance-task movement by two decades. He argued that tests measuring only recall cannot distinguish between understanding and memorization, and that real assessment requires students to transfer knowledge to novel contexts. This insight now underpins competency-based education, portfolio assessment, and the learning-objective architectures built into every modern LMS and AI tutoring platform.

Though Wiggins died in 2015, his influence persists in every curriculum that starts with standards and ends with performance tasks, in every EdTech product that maps activities to learning objectives, and in every teacher who asks "what evidence will I accept?" before planning a lesson.
